    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the tech giant "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the tech giant kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also stated that new export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    In a recent development, "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson stated in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    In a recent development, lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    Anthropic shares fall below IPO price. Traders see even more pain

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (376 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that anthropic shares are back trading below the IPO price after a 13% sell-off Tuesday and a 1.5% drop Monday, despite a broad rally in most major tech artificial intelligence names.
    • It took just four days for ANT to fall under its offering price, compared with 21 trading days for SpaceX, which rallied out of the gate.
    • Options volume on the stock is picking up as the shares drop and implied volatility jumps to 96, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic shares are back trading below the IPO price after a 13% sell-off Tuesday and a 1.5% drop Monday, despite a broad rally in most major tech artificial intelligence names. Trading under $76 on Tuesday, the stock's now 8.5% below its initial public offering level and 34% beneath its intraday high of $115.

    It took just four days for ANT to fall under its offering price, compared with 21 trading days for SpaceX, which rallied out of the gate.

    Options volume on the stock is picking up as the shares drop and implied volatility jumps to 96, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Almost 500,000 options traded by noon ET on Tuesday for a total premium of about $250 million, the sixth-most active single-stock options in the market, SpotGamma data shows.

    Almost 300,000 puts traded versus about 200,000 calls, but the sentiment implied by the trades was not overtly bearish, and judging by the biggest single trades of the day, traders are divided on what happens next.

    The biggest single option trade of the day was a $7.5 million purchase of almost 11,000 75-strike puts expiring in mid-December. The trader paid above the ask, suggesting an eagerness to get the trade done at a cost of $6.85, according to SpotGamma. With Anthropic trading at $77, the position needs Anthropic to drop 11% by expiry to pay off.

    "Anthropic remains bumpy as investors add risk to other names," said noted tech analyst Dan Ives.

    Industry observers note that only one obvious call purchase appeared among the top 10 trades: a 3,000-lot purchase of 85-strike calls expiring Jan. 15 that cost $7.10 each, for a total of $2.2 million. That trade needs Anthropic to rally 19% within the next two months to break even.

    In a recent development, arguably the most interesting action was a string of almost a dozen put sales, ranging from $400,000 to $1.6 million each, all within moments of each other, selling the 120-strike puts expiring Dec. 18. The puts bring in $40 each, meaning the breakeven for the trade is at $80. Selling in-the-money puts in high-volatility stocks is often a way for traders to get long stock without the capital requirements of buying the underlying equity.

    Donovan Mitchell on 9-9 Cavs' inconsistent effort: 'I'm trying to figure out how not to end up on ESPN'

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1488 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the Chicago Bulls entered Thanksgiving week as one of the NBA's worst teams: 4-12, getting outscored by nearly eight points per 100 possessions, with the second-worst defense in the NBA.
    • Sources indicate that this, despite the Cavs coming in with a rest advantage, with the Bulls on the second night of a back-to-back after going to overtime against the Nuggets on Sunday.
    • And, perhaps most importantly, despite the Cavs … well, frankly, they're just supposed to be better than this.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the Chicago Bulls entered Thanksgiving week as one of the NBA's worst teams: 4-12, getting outscored by nearly eight points per 100 possessions, with the second-worst defense in the NBA. And yet, they controlled the bulk of Monday's matchup with the Cleveland Cavaliers, leading for nearly the entire final three quarters — and by as many as 24 points — in a 122-108 win.

    Sources indicate that this, despite the Cavs coming in with a rest advantage, with the Bulls on the second night of a back-to-back after going to overtime against the Nuggets on Sunday. And despite Chicago being without leading scorer Norman Powell, who's stuck in street clothes nursing a strained right hamstring, and 2026 lottery pick Caleb Wilson, out with a broken right hand. And despite a pair of Chicago starters — point guard Josh Giddey and swingman Matas Buzelis — getting benched, again, late in the fourth quarter by first-year head coach Tiago Splitter, who elected to close with backup point guard Tre Jones and intriguing two-way reserve Jaylin Sellers. (Giddey did not seem particularly pleased about that.).

    And, perhaps most importantly, despite the Cavs … well, frankly, they're just supposed to be better than this.

    Donovan Mitchell (right), James Harden and the Cleveland Cavaliers have stumbled to .500 a month into the season.

    Sources indicate that yes, Cleveland's without Evan Mobley, an integral component of its operations on both sides of the floor. And yes, Kenny Atkinson's club wound up on the business end of Chicago going 20-for-49 from 3-point range while the Cavs made just eight of their 31 triple tries. Not exactly easy to win when you're outscored by 36 points from long distance.

    Sources indicate that it's not just the simple, cruel vicissitudes of shooting variance, though. Aside from Mobley, the Cavs had the entire rest of their preferred rotation against a four-win team … and they still got drilled. A Cleveland squad that made it to the Eastern Conference finals last spring enters Wednesday's matchup with the Newly introduced York Knicks — the team that, as you might recall, annihilated the Cavs in that series en route to winning the NBA championship — at 9-9, in seventh place in the East.

    That's a long way from where the Cavs — one of the most expensive rosters in the sport — want to be … and, from the sound of things, they've got some pretty big questions to answer before they can get there. From Danny Cunningham of The Inside Shot:.

    Donovan Mitchell, who had a game-high 28 points, was asked about the effort being inconsistent from quarter-to-quarter or game-to-game this season.

    Mitchell thought for a full five seconds after the question was asked.

    "I think," he noted before pausing for eight more seconds. "I'm trying to figure out how not to end up on ESPN.".

    In a recent development, "I think the biggest thing now is just figuring each other out. We're not here in the locker room panicking, and all I can say to that, is what we got going forward. Nights like tonight are bad. It's a bad night, and we got to respond to that. We've got to respond to that and just keep playing our game. There's so many different things you can point to, but at the end of the day for us, it's within us. I have all the confidence in everybody in here, and we've got all the confidence in each other. We've got to go out there and execute it. That doesn't really answer your question, but yeah.".

    It has been revealed that if there's one thing I'm qualified to assess as a longtime professional blogger, it's this: That was a lot of words to not really make any point or address the issue at hand. Which, come to think of it, might constitute a pretty loud statement about the state of affairs in Cleveland right about now.

    According to recent reports, mitchell wasn't the only Cavalier searching for an answer to the issues that have characterized the club's fits-and-starts opening to the season. Peyton Watson, the swingman who came over from Denver in an offseason sign-and-trade intended to plug Cleveland's long-yawning hole on the wing, offered a somewhat more direct answer than the All-NBA scoring guard.

    "I think if we knew the answer, we would just do it," Watson noted in the locker room. "I think we're still searching for that. You know, I'm always trying to communicate with my teammates and try to help make their job easier and just be a guy that connects the team in a lot of ways. I think I try to just go out there and lead by example by playing as hard as I can every night. I just think that everybody has got to look inward and look themselves in the mirror and ask themselves, 'Am I giving it 100% every single night?' I think that if that's not the case, then we need to go to the drawing board and really, like I said, look in the mirror and evaluate ourselves.".

    That doesn't exactly seem like the most stirring vote of confidence for the competitive makeup of the Cavaliers, especially considering they've already gone through a few moments that would seem to invite such sober self-reflection.

    Blowing a 29-point lead against the 76ers on opening night. Dropping both ends of a home-and-home to the post-injury-apocalypse Thunder. Getting boat-raced by the Knicks in the second half at home, an extension of the pain of the conference finals. Getting blown out by a Hornets team playing without Brandon Miller or Kon Knueppel. Getting out-executed down the stretch by a Grizzlies squad playing without Ty Jerome. And now, Monday's scattershot effort in Chicago.

    It just feels like something's missing in Cleveland, some spark, some urgency — and it starts on the defensive end.

    The last half-decade of success for the Cavs — a climb out of the post-LeBron basement that began with the Mobley/Allen/Darius Garland unit under J.B. Bickerstaff, and that continued after the trade for Mitchell made it a "core four" — had been predicated on consistently stout defenses, with Cleveland ranking in the top eight in points allowed per possession each season from 2021 through 2025. That began to shift when Atkinson's arrival supercharged the offense, and more firmly tilted after dealing for Harden; Cleveland posted a top-five offense after the trade deadline, but a below-average defense, and got routinely torched by the Knicks in the four-game conference finals sweep.

    The Cavs now sit at 21st in defensive efficiency — on pace for their first bottom-10 finish on that end since 2020-21. They're conceding shots at the rim and from beyond the 3-point line more regularly, and they give up wide-open 3s at a bottom-10 rate. (Nearly half of Chicago's 3-point attempts on Monday came without a Cavalier defender within 6 feet of the shooter.) They don't force turnovers, and they're average-at-best at clearing the defensive glass and guarding without fouling. That's a recipe for underwhelming results, unless you can balance out that bottom-10 defense with a No. 1-with-a-bullet offense … which the Cavs, at the moment a good-but-not-overwhelming seventh in points scored per possession, don't have at the moment.

    Maybe they will. Get Mobley healthy, get Harden — who followed up his 51-point Friday masterclass by shooting 5-for-14 from the floor with seven turnovers in Chicago — more consistently off the schneid, and get Watson (a career-low 48% on 2-pointers and 27% on 3s) thawed out, and maybe these Cavs have the ingredients they need to build on last season's trip to the final four and put themselves in position to make a bid to represent the East in the NBA Finals. They believe they have the talent to do that.

    Sources indicate that right now, though, they feel like a team that's less than the sum of its parts — a group that's playing like it's just kind of going through the motions until the real season starts, rather than one that needs to earn its postseason spot in an East that's gotten more crowded at the top. And if the Cavs want to have a shot at being the last team standing come springtime, they need to start finding answers as fall turns to winter.

    "You can't just turn it on in April or May," Cavs guard Sam Merrill told reporters. "I think building the right habits only makes it easier to play that way once you get to later in the season and in the playoffs. We continue to talk about it. That's got to continue to be our mindset.".

    Industry observers note that talking about it is one thing. Their next chance to do something about it comes Wednesday in Fresh York. One bit of good news for Mitchell and Co., at least? The game won't air on ESPN.

    #108624. Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a major win for the company and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    According to recent reports, adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and stated it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the massive indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    According to recent reports, "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he said.

    Part of the challenge, Niles noted, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    It has been revealed that "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he remarked, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    It has been revealed that anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan said. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the firm in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he stated. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    In a recent development, one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    How Meta is using Instagram to get an ad boost from its Muse personal AI agent

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Meta's ad-free Muse personal artificial intelligence agent is already helping the social media giant boost its advertising business, and it's happening through Instagram, multiple people told CNBC.
    • Instagram is a major advertising revenue engine for the social media giant, and the firm is leveraging existing habits on the platform by prompting users to organize their saved posts in Muse.
    • According to recent reports, about 20% of daily Instagram users save at least one post to the app per day, according to a person familiar with the details, who asked not to be named because the information is not public.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Meta's ad-free Muse personal artificial intelligence agent is already helping the social media giant boost its advertising business, and it's happening through Instagram, multiple people told CNBC.

    Instagram is a major advertising revenue engine for the social media giant, and the firm is leveraging existing habits on the platform by prompting users to organize their saved posts in Muse.

    According to recent reports, about 20% of daily Instagram users save at least one post to the app per day, according to a person familiar with the details, who asked not to be named because the information is not public. Many of those saved items, the person mentioned, are either shoppable items or ads.

    A senior executive told CNBC that Muse, even without ads, "is still very valuable for our ads business because it raises conversions for advertisers." It does this by reducing friction in the shopping process and allowing users to go back to items later, stated the executive, who asked not to be named because the details have not been reported publicly.

    "It gives advertisers a way to get more ROI for the dollars they're already spending, and that's all because Muse is helping people shop," the executive stated.

    It has been revealed that mark Zuckerberg announced in Meta's last earnings call that 25% of Muse's owners shop via the agentic tool — it's the most common use case for Muse — and the average purchase price is over $200. Zuckerberg mentioned the firm plans to take a small fee from transactions made through the agentic platform.

    In a recent development, all that information about what people are shopping for with their agent is a valuable asset to target ads more precisely within Instagram. If consumers complete purchases with their Muse, that builds Meta's new revenue stream.

    Meta's efforts to drive transactions seem to be paying off, and the buzz around Muse has made it a leader in agentic shopping.

    According to recent reports, in the week ending Nov. 22, 51% of all agentic orders were done by Meta's Muse, according to transactions measured by Forter Intelligence, an e-commerce analytics and cybertechnology manufacturer.

    Recent findings suggest that meta dominates agentic AI shopping market share, according to Forter, which remarked that SpaceX's Grok held a 24% market share in that same time period, followed by 22% to OpenAI's ChatGPT. The remaining 3% is divided between Google and startup Instinct.

    Meta is expected to eventually launch ads in Muse, though multiple people noted that it's not under any financial pressure to do so and tends to take its time building an audience before monetizing it.

    The people stated that putting ads in the Muse feed, which is more akin to a newsfeed instead of responses to specific queries, would be a natural way for Meta to test ads on the platform.

    #108619. Breaking: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    📅 16 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 30m • 📚 Deep Dive (5984 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

    📅 16 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 30 min read (5984 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert?
    • How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it?
    • Industry observers note that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the fresh signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

    How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

    Industry observers note that so what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

    Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

    According to recent reports, first Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

    Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N.

    Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

    “They are really good examples,” Arteta remarked. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

    “The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”.

    Recent findings suggest that you could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

    It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

    Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

    You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

    Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs.

    Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s newly introduced £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

    Recent findings suggest that when Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

    It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

    According to recent reports, city, in contrast to their opponents, indicated a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

    Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F.

    It has been revealed that it would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

    The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

    When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

    Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

    Recent findings suggest that in truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer plans remain up in the air for both camps.

    City appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

    Industry observers note that arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

    Recent findings suggest that although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the massive games is an area for improvement.

    The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

    Industry News: CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: AI race spreads from robots to smartphones

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing.
    • It has been revealed that I'm just back from APEC in Shenzhen, where I saw the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia gather along with other member economies.
    • It only took a few months for a humanoid robot to get better at picking up household items.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses.

    It has been revealed that I'm just back from APEC in Shenzhen, where I saw the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia gather along with other member economies. Beneath the fanfare, what's changed on the tech front in what's often dubbed China's Silicon Valley?

    It only took a few months for a humanoid robot to get better at picking up household items.

    Sources indicate that even after a human knocked a box and toys away from their original spots, a LimX robot swiftly located them and moved them to pre-set locations. While still far from perfect, the smoothness of the demo contrasted with the robot's more stilted movements I'd seen early this summer — and inability then to react to rapid changes in tasks.

    Sources indicate that when we caught up in Shenzhen last week, CFO Jesse Liu declined to comment on LimX's IPO looks. But he told me that his conversations around the APEC CEO Summit revealed an excitement around a new development for humanoids: growing demand for robot chips that can run smarter large language models locally, instead of on the cloud.

    "A lot of chipmakers are now happy about the latest developments in LLMs because they think robotic OEMs will actually begin to integrate more storage, and reasoning, and compute, and inference infrastructure on the edge, or locally inside the robot body," Liu mentioned, referring to original equipment manufacturers.

    "They do see robots moving from hundreds of units to thousands of units, to tens of thousands of units, beginning to enter that kind of automotive quantity," he mentioned, pointing to chip suppliers such as Horizon Robotics.

    New AI models, particularly GPT-6 Astra, have shown not just improved reasoning, but better control of robots.

    That puts more of the onus on hardware makers, for robots or other devices, to create practical applications. LimX mentioned it's working with business partners in over 30 markets, including Switzerland where the robots serve as power plant inspectors in rural areas.

    The key for powering AI's transition into the physical world is on-device chips and more powerful batteries. That means Nvidia's most expensive, cutting-edge chips won't be the only ones powering generative AI models.

    So far, even in basic consumer applications such as smartphones, AI isn't transformative enough to be a top-three selling point for mass-market users, Thomas Bai, AI product expert at smartphone company Honor, told me in Shenzhen.

    He expects that in the next few years, as smartphone chips are able to run more powerful AI models, the "super agent" tech can become better at completing tasks on its own, and anticipating a user's needs — such as ordering coffee.

    According to recent reports, counterpoint on Nov. 19 forecast that in the retail industry, "edge AI" revenue will surge sixfold by 2032, with roughly half of revenue coming from retail robots that clean and check inventory — often with the help of smaller AI models that can run on locally embedded chips.

    But more capable, on-device AI also requires more battery power, Honor's Bai pointed out.

    Honor's X70 Android smartphone, which introduced last summer, boasts a battery with 8,300 milliampere-hours for a total device weight of just under 200 grams. That compares with 5,000 mAH for the 214-gram flagship Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and roughly 5,400 mAH for this year's 249-gram Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max, according to GSM Arena.

    LimX's Oli humanoid comes with 9,500 mAH battery capacity, lasting the robot about 1.5 hours.

    Such AI applications, however, remain sensitive to the memory-chip shortage weighing on the industry.

    The X70 was the best-selling Android phone in the entry to mid-tier range, said Shenzhen-based Counterpoint analyst Shiwen Ma.

    While Ma said penetration of smartphones with generative AI features is higher in China at 55% versus 38% overseas, the offerings are still not essential to users, while rising memory-chip costs make it harder for manufacturers to bring AI-powered devices to the mass market.

    Geely-backed automotive tech company EcarX's CFO Dylan Jeng told me earlier this month he expects the memory price surge to persist through 2027, and even the first half of 2028.

    The chipmaker that can narrow the gap for on-device AI needs could find its moment soon.

    Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged.

    U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke exclusively on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." President Donald Trump on Friday said he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week.

    How China is using summits to expand its global influence.

    According to recent reports, for a second year in a row, Xi has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores. But U.S.-China trade, Taiwan and tech tensions remain unresolved as Trump returned from Asia.

    Putin scores 'massive win' at first trilateral meeting.

    In a recent development, the first-ever three-way summit is "arguably a diplomatic victory for Moscow," said Andrius Tursa, an advisor for Central and Eastern Europe and Russia at Teneo. The view from inside the APEC welcome banquet showed the leaders were in close proximity from the start of the summit.

    Nov. 27: Industrial profits (Oct).

    According to recent reports, nov. 27 - Dec. 6: Guangzhou auto show.

    Breaking: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a substantial buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (408 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    Sources indicate that anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," said Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, fresh technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    The Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    In her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the big losses.

    In a recent development, the fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    Industry observers note that "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she said. "That's how crazy things were.".

    Industry News: As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the newly introduced tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Industry observers note that implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders big and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," stated Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shares of Anthropic closed down 6.5% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the artificial intelligence organization's $83 IPO price.
    • Sources indicate that the AI lab's stock has been sinking steadily since opening at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest offering of all time.
    • In a recent development, chip stocks Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Intel, as well as neoclouds CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius, all fell during intraday trading on Tuesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of Anthropic closed down 6.5% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the artificial intelligence organization's $83 IPO price.

    Sources indicate that the AI lab's stock has been sinking steadily since opening at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest offering of all time. Investors eagerly awaited Anthropic's debut in hopes that the firm would revitalize the broader AI trade, which has been volatile in recent weeks over concerns about the feasibility of a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure buildout.

    In a recent development, chip stocks Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Intel, as well as neoclouds CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius, all fell during intraday trading on Tuesday. The market is still reeling after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a dramatic reversal from his ouster earlier this month. Nvidia shares surged more than 30% on Monday, but pared those gains Tuesday.

    In a recent development, analysts at Canaccord Genuity said Tuesday that they're focused on Anthropic's long-term potential. They said they believe that the company is building "one of the most key enterprise technology franchises of the AI era" and that the "opportunity is considerably larger than traditional software spending.".

    Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and a $135 price target.

    "The risks are unusually large, particularly around infrastructure commitments and the durability of competitive differentiation, but we believe the combination of exceptional growth, emerging earnings capacity, and an attractive entry valuation support a compelling investment opportunity," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note.

    Wedbush analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating and a $120 price target on Monday. They stated Anthropic went public in a "tumultuous market" as debate around the AI buildout continues, but that they expect the tech giant to navigate the competitive environment and "capture a uniquely large addressable market.".

    "While there's going to continue to be many ups and downs, and winners and losers as this ecosystem gets built, in our view there is no real question that it does get built over time," the analysts wrote in a Monday note. "The genie is out of the bottle. And ANT is a strong play on that theme.".

    Analysts at Oppenheimer initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating on Tuesday, and they set a $150 price target for the stock.

    According to recent reports, they said their "bullish stance" on the organization stems from their belief that Anthropic will capture growing enterprise AI spending, that its improving compute efficiency lowers cost per task and that its multi-chip strategy optimizes price performance. The analysts added that Anthropic's focus on the enterprise also relies less on consumer subsidies, and that rising customer adoption creates "a substantial runway" for the company.

    "While competition and compute commitments remain risks, we believe Anthropic can translate its leadership into durable growth and operating leverage," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note.

    Consumer confidence shoots up after Democrats' midterm victories — though inflation worries persist

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (311 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Consumers grew significantly more optimistic in November in the wake of the midterm elections, with a growing number of Americans now seeing improvement in the labor market and expecting inflation to cool.
    • The Conference Board survey released Tuesday showed improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3, up 11.4 points from October and much better than the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 92.2.
    • In a recent development, confidence among Democrats and independent voters improved sharply, the Conference Board remarked, while confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Consumers grew significantly more optimistic in November in the wake of the midterm elections, with a growing number of Americans now seeing improvement in the labor market and expecting inflation to cool.

    The Conference Board survey released Tuesday showed improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3, up 11.4 points from October and much better than the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 92.2.

    In a recent development, confidence among Democrats and independent voters improved sharply, the Conference Board remarked, while confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly. Still, confidence among Republicans remained the highest among the three groups.

    While respondents "continued to express frustration with high prices and rising costs," they also "cited hope for the general economy," said Fergus McCormick, the board's senior economist for global indicators.

    The survey comes with the Federal Reserve continuing to try to bring down inflation, which has run above the central bank's 2% target for some 5½ years. The Fed is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point when it meets again in two weeks.

    Despite the lingering worries about the cost of living — a centerpiece issue during the midterms — the survey's present situation and expectations indexes both posted strong gains. Inflation expectations for 12 months from now fell for the second straight month but remained high at 5.7%.

    Industry observers note that the survey's closely watched gap between jobs considered "plentiful" versus "hard to get" widened to 12.4 percentage points. The "plentiful" side rose to 30.8% from 26.2% while "hard to get" fell to 18.4%, down 3 percentage points.

    The survey results are the second in the past week to reveal that Americans are growing more optimistic about the economy. The University of Michigan's November survey, released Friday, showed a 7.3% increase since October, with a similar partisan split.

    #108580. Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1092 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones mentioned directors did not intend to reinstate him.
    • Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.
    • The reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the company reported strong third-quarter results.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones mentioned directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back.

    Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.

    The reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the company reported strong third-quarter results. A petition calling for Huang's return had drawn more than 200,000 signatures, according to its organizers.

    The rally spread across the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.5% and the S&P 500 rising 4.7%, each posting its strongest session since April 2025.

    Industry observers note that nvidia's board mentioned it had received input from senior U.S. government officials and that its investigation into Huang's conduct would continue.

    Still, the board's reversal, President Donald Trump's administration's role and continued scrutiny of Nvidia's China business leave major questions for both investors and lawmakers.

    In a recent development, sen. Jack Reed, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, urged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Monday to appear before the committee to discuss the case.

    Reed did not lay out a specific list of questions for the two officials, but his statement cited reporting that Trump had been briefed by intelligence officials led by then-National Security Adviser Marco Rubio before intervening in support of Huang's return.

    Reed's call adds to mounting pressure on both Nvidia and the Trump administration to explain what they knew and when.

    Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., vice ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, remarked Huang’s reinstatement could broaden congressional scrutiny rather than bring it to a close.

    “I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query,” Amo told CNBC, adding that lawmakers should also examine administration officials involved in decisions affecting Nvidia and chip sales to China.

    In a recent development, amo said he expects the planned closed-door interview with Huang on Dec. 1 to proceed and that Congress would continue seeking answers both privately and publicly in the coming months.

    “He should start purchasing his plane tickets to Washington,” he said. “It is abundantly clear that this is ripe for questioning by Congress.”.

    On Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, Jones said the board had accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him.

    Less than a week later, the board reversed course, saying Monday that it had unanimously voted to bring Huang back after discussions with him and input from senior U.S. government officials.

    Trump said he had spoken with board members and that his administration provided assurances based on the information available to it. But the board has not publicly detailed what it was told.

    "The board decided to do what we wanted to do," Trump told CNBC, adding that he believed his intervention had been important.

    "I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it," he said.

    Trump also called into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's return, Semafor reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

    Reed has called on Huang to disclose his communications with Trump and on Nvidia to release a transcript of the board's call with the president.

    Lawmakers are still seeking answers about the alleged smuggling of Nvidia products to China, their possible diversion for military use and possible advancement of Chinese AI capabilities.

    The Senate Banking Committee has scheduled Huang to testify on U.S. export controls on Dec. 3. House lawmakers have also confirmed closed-door interviews with Huang on Dec. 1 and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2.

    Sources indicate that "The Nvidia board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," Reps. John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford and Brian Mast stated in a joint statement.

    Their inquiry may also examine what Nvidia knew about the customers and resellers involved, as well as what controls the firm had in place.

    Recent findings suggest that other lawmakers have also sought to preserve the paper trail. Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons had asked senior administration officials on Nov. 11 to retain records related to Nvidia exports of advanced AI chips to China and associated national security concerns.

    Sources indicate that nvidia has promised to hire a chief compliance officer and establish a committee overseeing national security and export controls. The board's investigation into Huang's conduct also remains underway.

    Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for APAC and the Middle East, stated investors will be watching whether those new safeguards carry meaningful authority.

    Succession remains another question.

    Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said Nvidia has a limited window to prepare for the possibility that a future president may be less supportive of Huang.

    With Trump's term ending in two years, Luria argued that Nvidia needs a clearer plan for who could take over if Huang were forced to leave again.

    It has been revealed that gilbert pointed to Nvidia's roughly 75% revenue-growth forecast for the next financial year as evidence of strong near-term demand. The longer-term question, he remarked, is whether customer orders and artificial intelligence investment can sustain that pace.

    Luria told CNBC that concerns about the broader AI trade remain, including the cost of financing data centers, potential overbuilding by neocloud companies and obstacles to building latest facilities.

    Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon said worries about whether AI spending is achievable and sustainable were not caused solely by Huang's departure. UBS, meanwhile, flagged Nvidia's roughly $390 billion in supply commitments and the need to keep demand flowing through its ecosystem.

    It has been revealed that gilbert stated part of Monday's rally reflected investors recovering earlier losses rather than pricing in upcoming growth. Bernstein restored its "Outperform" rating and kept its $200 price target, while UBS maintained its $220 target.

    "For the share price, it comes down to whether Nvidia can keep delivering as it has done over recent years," noted Gilbert, adding that Huang's return could ease some concerns about Nvidia's longer-term outlook.

    Recent findings suggest that "The real worry has been what happens beyond next year. Having Huang back at the helm goes a long way to easing those concerns, because he's the one who sits down with the biggest customers and gets those multi-year orders over the line," he noted.

    — CNBC's David Sucherman, Justin Papp and Eko Prasetyo contributed to the story.

    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    Recent findings suggest that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    According to recent reports, on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note mentioned.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    In that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Breaking: Gold is doing something strange. Here's one way to play it

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (914 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that gold has stopped trading like a haven and started trading more like a market index this year.
    • It has been revealed that over long timeframes, gold's returns tend to move independently of the S&P 500's.
    • According to recent reports, the options market is also behaving unusually.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that gold has stopped trading like a haven and started trading more like a market index this year. The past week has underscored it. Fears around AI, a hawkish Fed, and a stronger dollar sent many investors rushing to raise cash, and gold was sold along with stocks. GLD (SPDR Gold Shares) and the S&P 500 both slid around 9%. Gold then shared in the market's Monday rebound, with GLD up about 3% as the S&P 500 jumped nearly 5%.

    It has been revealed that over long timeframes, gold's returns tend to move independently of the S&P 500's. From 2004 to 2025, the correlation between their daily returns has been just 0.05 (+1 means the two move in lockstep and -1 means they move in opposite directions). That relationship fluctuates, and 2026 has seen an unusually strong link. The correlation has been about 0.41 so far in 2026. Its rolling three-month reading peaked near 0.80 in June and now sits at 0.54, still higher than about 95% of rolling three-month readings since 2005. Since the end of August, GLD has fallen on 77% of the S&P 500's down days, compared with roughly half historically.

    According to recent reports, the options market is also behaving unusually. Gold options typically price calls richer than puts (call skew). Like other commodities, gold is prone to sharp rallies, and investors use calls to bet on them or hedge against macroeconomic risks. However, gold options have mostly shown the reverse this year, with puts at the moment trading richer than calls (put skew). It's a sign investors are paying a premium for protection against further declines, which is unusual for gold and more typical of stock options.

    It has been revealed that those richer puts come as uncertainty around gold runs high heading into December. The PCE inflation report arrives Wednesday, followed by the jobs report next week and the Fed's decision and CPI the week after. GLD's implied volatility, a measure of how much the options market expects the fund to move, is now higher than on about 80% of days over the past year. Options are pricing in an expected move of about 6%, or roughly $20, by Dec. 18. With gold options pricier than usual and puts unusually rich, that presents an interesting setup for traders willing to sell premium.

    Industry observers note that based on Monday's close, I'm selling the Dec. 18 310/300 put spread and 360/370 call spread in GLD for a credit of roughly $2.24.

    This is a directionally neutral trade. Gold has been swinging with the market and is down about 33% from its January high. With the Fed and inflation data ahead, it's hard to say whether gold has bottomed or has further to fall into mid-December. A neutral position can collect the elevated premium without picking a direction, and the richer put side adds more.

    The short strikes sit just outside the range the options market is pricing for Dec. 18, roughly 7% to 8% from Monday's close. That leaves room for a continued selloff or an extended rebound. The trade reaches its maximum profit of $224 if GLD closes between $310 and $360 on Dec. 18. It carries a 62% theoretical probability of profit and can show a gain before expiration if GLD remains relatively rangebound.

    Recent findings suggest that the maximum loss is capped by the long options and reaches $776 if GLD closes below $300 or above $370, 10% to 11% from Monday's close. Defining risk is especially crucial with the upcoming catalysts and recent price volatility in gold. GLD has had 30 daily moves of more than 3% this year, including a 10.3% drop on Jan. 30. The trade breaks even at $307.76 on the downside and $362.24 on the upside.

    Industry observers note that A close between $360 and $370 can assign the short call and leave a short position in the fund, so investors looking to avoid that should consider managing the trade before expiration. If GLD finishes between $300 and $310, the short put can be assigned, creating an obligation to buy 100 shares per spread at $310. After the credit, that's a cost basis of about $307.76, roughly 8% below Monday's close.

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Trump Account contributions from friends and family pass $1 billion mark, Treasury says

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Families and friends have collectively contributed more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts since the July 4 launch, bringing total deposits to more than $9 billion, the U.S.
    • Recent findings suggest that the $1 billion in Trump Account deposits come from more than 3 million individuals, according to the agency.
    • "The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character," U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Families and friends have collectively contributed more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts since the July 4 launch, bringing total deposits to more than $9 billion, the U.S. Department of the Treasury mentioned Tuesday in an announcement exclusively provided to CNBC.

    Recent findings suggest that the $1 billion in Trump Account deposits come from more than 3 million individuals, according to the agency. That total does not include the government's seed money or philanthropic gifts from donors such as Michael and Susan Dell.

    "The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted in a written statement.

    It has been revealed that "Trump Accounts are a transformative government program for American children. It is the largest government start-up in American history," Internal Revenue Service CEO Frank Bisignano said in the statement.

    Recent findings suggest that also known as 530A accounts, Trump Accounts are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number.

    Industry observers note that parents, guardians, grandparents and others can collectively contribute up to $5,000 per child per year in after-tax dollars up until the year before the beneficiary turns 18. The annual contribution limit is indexed for inflation after 2027.

    Children born from 2025 through 2028 may receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury. Other funds may also be available, depending on certain criteria.

    Most recently, Snowflake chairman Frank Slootman and his wife, Brenda, confirmed they would give $1,000 to every child in Montana born in 2023 and 2024.

    The Treasury rolled out temporary regulations at the end of September that allow Trump Accounts to hold stock donations, a move meant to pave the way for more philanthropic gifts, according to Bisignano.

    These rules make it more attractive for donors, according to Ben Henry-Moreland, a certified financial planner with advisor platform Kitces.com.

    Industry observers note that by gifting stocks, wealthy founders and shareholders can avoid the capital gains taxes that would otherwise be triggered by selling appreciated stock and donating the cash proceeds. However, it also means some children's wealth accumulation could be tied to the performance of individual companies.

    The Trump Accounts milestone comes as more billionaires and companies pledge support to the investment account for kids.

    In an exclusive interview with CNBC's "Squawk on the Street," Bessent on Nov. 20 confirmed an Anthropic co-founder would make a "large gift" to Trump Accounts over the next few weeks.

    According to recent reports, A person briefed on the announcement confirmed that the Anthropic co-founder Bessent referred to is Tom Brown and that it is part of his broader philanthropic plan. The person asked not to be named because the matter is private.

    "This is the perfect vehicle to donate to the children of America, and they will receive 100% of the proceeds," Bessent noted.

    Elon Musk wrote in an X post that he plans to give every kid in America a share of SpaceX sometime in 2027, which experts say may come via Trump Accounts.

    In a separate funding announcement, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said she would donate around 2 million shares of her and her husband's SpaceX stock to the accounts.

    On Monday, Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, founder of Invest America and an architect of Trump Accounts, told CNBC's "Halftime Report" that more large-scale donations may be in the pipeline.

    "I want everybody to own shares of Nvidia, in Anthropic, in OpenAI," he said. "We created 70 million stock accounts — free stock accounts — for every single citizen under the age of 18 to do just that, and we have huge announcements coming.".

    Jensen Huang to face DC grilling the same day Nvidia releases fresh products at GTC

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1128 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of Nvidia, and is now tasked with selling the firm's artificial intelligence vision while also defending himself in Washington.
    • As Nvidia employees celebrated the return of their leader to the company's headquarters, Huang told the gathered crowd, "I'll be a better CEO the second time around.".
    • Huang will need to be a better CEO to head off the concerns surrounding Nvidia and the broader AI industry exposed by Huang's exit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang is back as the CEO of Nvidia, and is now tasked with selling the firm's artificial intelligence vision while also defending himself in Washington.

    As Nvidia employees celebrated the return of their leader to the company's headquarters, Huang told the gathered crowd, "I'll be a better CEO the second time around.".

    Huang will need to be a better CEO to head off the concerns surrounding Nvidia and the broader AI industry exposed by Huang's exit. The challenges include a proliferating roster of investigations and hearings from Congress, regulators and state-level officials, as well as technical and competitive questions about how long Nvidia's currently dominant graphics processing units can remain on top.

    In a recent development, "There's nothing prohibiting him from doing what he does on his day job," mentioned Katten chair and former federal prosecutor Gil Soffer. But investigations take significant prep time, Soffer said. "You don't just walk in cold.".

    Sources indicate that at Nvidia's GTC conference in Washington, D.C., next week, the organization will attempt to convince customers, partners and suppliers that it is developing the future of AI. At the same time, lawmakers will be pressing its newly reinstated CEO over what he knew and when about Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.

    Sources indicate that huang, before his scandals, was scheduled to give the GTC DC keynote speech on Dec. 1 to discuss latest Nvidia products and the trajectory of the AI ecosystem. In the past, the two-hour speech was the highlight of the event with hordes of fans full of the Huang-inspired "Jensanity.".

    "People will want to see that it's business as usual, which hopefully for Nvidia shareholders will mean that Jensen Huang confirms some new exciting products," said Babson College associate professor Peter Cohan.

    Sources indicate that right now, Nvidia has Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, filling the slot. A representative for Nvidia declined to answer multiple questions about whether Huang would appear at the firm's event.

    On the same day, Huang is scheduled to speak with three House committees — Foreign Affairs, Select Committee on the CCP, and the Select Committee on Intelligence — behind closed doors, where his interview will be transcribed.

    According to recent reports, "The NVIDIA board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," the chairs stated in a joint statement. They said that Huang has confirmed he will appear for the transcribed interview on Dec. 1.

    Next Tuesday's interviews are just the first of a slew of investigations.

    In a recent development, on Dec. 3, just as Nvidia's conference is wrapping up, the Senate Banking Committee will hold a hearing titled "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls." Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., who chairs the committee, said Huang will publicly testify as the sole witness.

    California's attorney general is also investigating Huang's remarks, and politicians from the Senate Finance, Intelligence, and Foreign Relations committees have inquired about the scandal. In the House, Energy and Commerce has requested a organization briefing from Nvidia, in addition to the three committees mentioned earlier. That's not counting an investigation from the Department of Justice and a reported investigation from the Securities and Exchange Commission.

    Plus, Huang still has to cooperate with an investigation from the board of directors, led by the law firm Wachtell Lipton.

    Meanwhile, Nvidia needs Huang to reassure investors and the broader AI ecosystem that the manufacturer is developing new products that will be in high demand. Investors had stated that while Nvidia's products for the next two years have been fully designed, they were worried that the chipmaker's pace of innovation would slow without Huang.

    It has been revealed that nvidia is facing fresh competition from chips from its biggest customers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Amazon and Microsoft. The companies have been developing their own chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia, as well as to control AI costs.

    "There was already this worry that we're spending too much on it," said Stephanie Balaouras, vice president of group research at Forrester. "One of those cost management strategies is to match ... the workload requirements to the right infrastructure. You don't need to put everything on a Nvidia GPU.".

    Many in the AI industry see Huang as one of the staunchest defenders of "open-source" AI that is free to use for commercial purposes, as compared with "frontier models" from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, which charge consumers by the token.

    Industry observers note that nvidia has also been spending heavily to develop its own open-source models called Nemotron. Presently, Nvidia Vice President Kari Briski is scheduled to present new Nemotron technology at GTC.

    On Monday, Nvidia's board stated that "senior levels" of the U.S. government provided input on Huang's potential national security risk. President Donald Trump told CNBC that he was central to convincing Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang and said he gave the board assurances.

    Trump's help could draw even more scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, who were already focused on probing Nvidia's chip sales.

    "Today's news that Donald Trump engineered the rehiring of Jensen Huang at Nvidia is Exhibit A about the political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration's major tech and AI policy," stated Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland in a call with reporters Monday.

    It has been revealed that republicans have also criticized Huang's return as the focus on the company's China sales intensifies. Still, the investigations could start to weigh on Nvidia's CEO, experts say.

    "How could he possibly do the job?" Jeff Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean at the Yale School of Management, told CNBC, citing Senate investigations, House investigations and other state investigations, even before Democrats take over next year.

    And the reaction in Washington to Huang's scandal could start to affect Nvidia's sales.

    Last week, the Department of Commerce declared that it will prevent Chinese companies from getting around export controls by renting Nvidia's chips across borders. On Monday, Commerce also added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist.

    And it's not just Nvidia that is relying on a strong performance from Huang. The organization's investors, customers, partners and shareholders will also look to see if Nvidia still wants to be at the center of the AI ecosystem. Before Huang was removed, he pushed Nvidia to invest in AI startups, while selling them products, and helping finance their infrastructure.

    Remarks from Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress last week while she was interim CEO suggested that Nvidia would be taking a "very strong look" at using its balance sheet to support the AI ecosystem, but it's unclear if Huang's second stint as CEO will continue with his prior showmanship or abide by a more measured approach.

    Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
