    The biggest money-making energy trade looks over. What to buy instead

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1777 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Is one of the greatest money-making trades of the last few years coming to an end?
    • No, I'm not talking about Nvidia or any of the data center- or AI-related power companies (although they have been crushed lately too… more on that on CNBC TV.
    • I'm talking about whether the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    What I'm hearing from energy insiders.

    Is one of the greatest money-making trades of the last few years coming to an end?

    No, I'm not talking about Nvidia or any of the data center- or AI-related power companies (although they have been crushed lately too… more on that on CNBC TV. Tune in!).

    I'm talking about whether the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding. Over the last year, the jump in some of these companies has been nothing short of remarkable.

    That jump is largely due to massive increases in margins, earnings, and cash flow. Those have occurred because of a major jump in what is called a crack spread. That is the difference between the price of oil and the finished price of refined products such as diesel and jet fuel. For most of this year, spreads have been soaring as disruptions and attacks on facilities and shipping in the Arabian Gulf, Hormuz, and deep inside Russia have played havoc with the market. In the last week or so, however, something big has changed: many of those spreads have started to tighten.

    This seismic drop in spreads is causing a selloff in the aforementioned refinery companies.

    If spreads continue to fall, these stocks may well keep selling off from recent highs. The upshot for investors may be that, as the shares come down, analysts see more upside. The median price target for Phillips 66 (PSX) now indicates a 20% gain from here, while smaller-cap Par Pacific (PARR) is double that.

    Here are a few other key points to focus on heading into the Thanksgiving-shortened week.

    I like to keep politics as much at arm's length as possible — we all know that energy and politics (sadly) often go hand in hand. Energy policies coming from Washington, D.C., can drive — or destroy — investment dollars. With all the substantial shifts in the White House over the last 10 years (four years of Trump, four years of Biden, and now 2 years into Trump #2), energy policies can blow through Washington faster than a summer squall hits a wind turbine. But because federal policies can mean so much for specific companies, sectors, and investments, it's vital to follow the news flow.

    That said, I'd like to take a moment to introduce you to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, known as BAAJA (and pronounced like the state in Mexico). Like much legislation, BAAJA is an obscure but important bill working its way through the American Congress. BAAJA does a lot of things, but what Power Insider readers care about is its focus on energy permitting reform. In a nutshell, BAAJA would help speed up the building of fresh electricity infrastructure. Again, that's an overly simplistic view of a major bill, but it needs to be on your radar. The utility trade group Edison Electric Institute came out in favor of the legislation this month after the industry received some 11th-hour changes. See more about it in our recent interview with EEI President Drew Maloney here.

    The bill passed the U.S. Senate in a vote late Thursday night. Now it moves to the House. Support for its final passage is also coming from the major LNG trade group, whose executive director said he "applauds the Senate for its bipartisan effort to pass meaningful, bipartisan, and durable permitting reforms aimed at delivering greater predictability, consistency, and certainty in the permitting, production, and export process for U.S. LNG. This legislation moves us closer to untangling red tape and eliminating overlapping agency reviews that can keep U.S. energy projects delayed for years.".

    Sources indicate that the Natural Gas Supply Association also chimed in, saying it urges Congress to see the bill as "a resource-agnostic and balanced reform agenda for boosting American energy security. It keeps strong environmental reviews in place, but it draws a firm line against the endless procedural delays that tie critical energy projects in knots for a decade.".

    Industry observers note that in my view, passing BAAJA is an important test of Congress's appetite for helping the energy and electrical power industry, lowering costs, and speeding time to market. The old adage was correct: time is money. Literally. If BAAJA moves on through the House, we could see an upside move in some utility stocks and any tech giant related to energy infrastructure.

    Industry observers note that speaking of politics, the news is getting lost in the massive Anthropic (ANT) IPO, but the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) — whose importance I wrote about in the last edition — just decided to resume permitting for data centers. The Texas Tribune did a nice write-up on it, and you can read it here.

    According to recent reports, it's tough to say, but it's true. The two are inextricably linked by policies created at both the federal and state levels. As I wrote in the last edition, some federally elected officials may have less impact on state-level issues — like the data center buildout — but they certainly have power over national laws. While many of you are enthralled, disgusted, or confused by sordid tales of Nvidia and Jensen-gate, keep one eye open on what happens in Washington, D.C.

    Have a great week, and have a wonderful Thanksgiving, everyone.

    Perhaps the substantial investor story — which is, like most things lately, related to Jensen-gate and Nvidia—is the sizable selloff in many AI, neocloud, and data center power-related stocks.

    Painful for current shareholders, but significant drops can also bring big opportunities. Wall Street believes that's the case, at least right now. Look at some of the potential upside based on the stocks' prices versus their price targets.

    We spoke with the CEO of Applied Digital (APLD) about all of this on CNBC last week, and you can watch it here. He highlighted how the market may be getting these stock stories wrong because, at least with his firm, he has long-term contracts with solid-credit companies. In that way, Applied Digital is more like a landlord than a "pure-play" AI company.

    Industry observers note that my take → While I'm not going to recommend a specific stock, I would add that it is critical for investors to understand the differences between these companies. While they may have some things in common, they are also different, with different business models, customers, leases, and sources of revenue.

    Speaking of recommendations… here are two ideas for you:.

    Recent findings suggest that A recent decline presents a nice opportunity in SOLV Energy (MWH). UBS analyst Jon Windham upgrades SOLV to buy from neutral, believing the market is "underappreciating several key tailwinds for SOLV given uncertainty around data center demand and higher interest rates." UBS highlights how the stock has fallen lately despite making two deals and beating and raising recent guidance. UBS claims now is an "attractive entry point" for SOLV. (Side note: MWH is a great stock ticker.).

    It has been revealed that while markets overall fall, BMO remains bullish on Bloom Energy (BE). After speaking with the firm, the analyst is upgrading Bloom to outperform, saying he remains "increasingly confident of BE's commercial traction" and that he still has conviction even with the recent drop in shares. While analyst Ameet Thakkar did cut his target to $230 from $260, that's still 50% upside from the current price. Bloom shares have tumbled 45% since October 1.

    Recent findings suggest that I was recently asked for my opinion on the price of oil. Here's my take. The market clearly wants to push oil contract prices lower and has for a few months. But, as I've said and reported for a while, don't confuse the futures (paper) price with the actual price. Yes, shipping rates and insurance rates have come down from recent highs — and there is a good amount of oil now flowing through Hormuz — but the cost of a physical barrel of crude is still well above the futures contract. If we get real, longer-lasting peace around Iran, oil prices will fall. There is plenty of oil in the world. That said, if bombs and missiles start firing again, oil prices will firm. I know that's a non-answer answer, but the oil market is truly headline-driven right now. My late good friend Boone Pickens (later in life, he didn't like being called by the "T" in his first name) used to avoid giving a set price target and instead give a directional quote, so I'll do the same: the odds of oil being lower in two months than it is today are 75%.

    Sources indicate that last week, I had a one-on-one with Vimal Kapur, chair and CEO of Honeywell International (HON), at an RBC conference in New York City. While the conversation wasn't filmed, I can tell you that Kapur offered investors reassurance that his order book is doing very, very well. This is important because Honeywell is huge in the things that make other things work. Its sensors go into a ton of energy facilities, from refineries to LNG facilities. Honeywell is a leading indicator of spending and buildouts, so if it keeps getting orders, it's a good sign for macro energy.

    Bottom line: Watch Honeywell stock as a potential "tell.".

    In a recent development, this week's Inside Line interview takes a different approach. We hit our friend Craig Johnson up for actionable insights into energy and stocks. Craig is managing director and chief market technician at Piper Sandler. He recently appeared on Power Lunch to talk about markets and stocks. He mentioned being bullish on energy, so we wanted to dig in just a little bit more.

    Sources indicate that this week, we had the pleasure of chatting with Balaji Krishnamurthy, president of Chevron Australia. We spoke at length about natural gas, the impact of disruptions, and long-term demand from Chevron customers in the Asia-Pacific region.

    This is a bit of a local RBI for the Newly introduced York City area, but one I felt was important to highlight. New York's electric grid operator just came out with a massive warning for everyone in our region: in just a couple of years, there may not be enough electricity supply to power our needs. A new report indicates a deficit in seven years, with a nearly 2 GW power hole in a decade. That's a number of big power plants' worth of energy. Get your solar panels on and buy that backup generator! I'll call this one random, but scary.

    Catch up with more on energy including interviews and video content from CNBC and Power Insider.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, it's Thanksgiving week in the NFL and there's a lot to go over, both on the injury front and the schedule.
    • So Week 12 is spread across five different days, which can be pretty hectic for fantasy football managers.
    • Herbert: The Chargers have shown signs of life over the past two weeks, scoring 23 and 24 points, respectively.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, it's Thanksgiving week in the NFL and there's a lot to go over, both on the injury front and the schedule. The Packers and Rams play Wednesday night, while we have the usual three-game Thanksgiving lineup. We also have the Broncos and Steelers on Black Friday, then the normal Sunday slate and Monday Night Football.

    So Week 12 is spread across five different days, which can be pretty hectic for fantasy football managers. We're here to help out, taking you through the NFL injury report with the latest updates and some fantasy analysis for key players.

    Justin Herbert, LAC (concussion protocol).

    Drake Maye, NE (leg) — Out at least six weeks.

    Herbert: The Chargers have shown signs of life over the past two weeks, scoring 23 and 24 points, respectively. Herbert turned in his first QB1 finish of the 2026 season with 22.44 fantasy points against the Jets on Sunday. He only had 131 passing yards, two TDs, 32 rushing yards and another score on the ground, so it isn't like "we are so back" or anything. But now Herbert will need to clear concussion protocol in order to play Week 12 against the Patriots, another solid matchup.

    With how the QB landscape is right now, if Herbert can clear, he isn't a bad add as a QB2 or streaming option for Week 12. The Chargers have some winnable matchups down the stretch and Herbert will likely need to throw. Maybe Herbert and the Chargers can still salvage something for fantasy.

    It has been revealed that darnold: The reigning Super Bowl champ has missed the past two games but has a shot to get back on the field for Week 12 against the 49ers in a massive spot. Seattle is coming off its bye and Drew Lock has been the starter. He's been more than serviceable, undefeated in essentially four starts this season. There's not much difference between Darnold and Lock starting for fantasy managers. Whoever starts will be a QB2 this week, and either way, Jaxon Smith-Njigba will get fed.

    Bhayshul Tuten, JAX (lower body).

    Josh Jacobs, GB (finger) — Unlikely to play in Week 12.

    J.K. Dobbins, DEN (suspension) — Won't play in Week 12.

    Walker: The Chiefs' lead back missed his second straight game Sunday, though the team didn't miss him much. Kansas City rolled to another easy win over the Cardinals, 34-7. Emmett Johnson led the backfield again with another strong performance, racking up 143 total yards, four catches and a score for 22.3 fantasy points. Johnson has RB1 finishes in three of his past four games.

    The Chiefs take on the Bills in a highly anticipated matchup on Thanksgiving night. Walker will have a short week to get ready to return, which isn't ideal. He was limited at practice on Tuesday. If Walker sits again, Johnson can be fired up as an RB1 in what should be a high-scoring affair. If Walker is able to play, we could see him eased back into action given how well Johnson has fared in his stead. In that scenario, Walker would return to RB1/2 status while Johnson would hold value as a flex play.

    Sources indicate that tuten: The Jaguars took a tough loss in Week 11 to the Giants and lost Tuten late in the game with an undisclosed injury. He had been dealing with an ankle glitch coming into the contest, so it could have something to do with that. Either way, Tuten has been playing pretty banged up over the last handful of games.

    In a recent development, if Tuten ends up missing Week 12, Chris Rodriguez Jr. would likely take over the backfield. He had four carries for 28 yards against Newly introduced York, and has four rushing TDs on the season. C-Rod would basically be elevated to RB2 status with a matchup against the Titans in Week 12. If Tuten is active, you have to play him but know there's some risk given the injuries.

    Davante Adams, LAR (hamstring) — Out until at least Week 13.

    Marvin Harrison Jr., HOU (hamstring).

    It has been revealed that A.J. Brown, NE (hamstring) — Likely out.

    Sources indicate that bowers: The Raiders were without their top offensive weapon for a loss to the Broncos on Sunday afternoon in Week 11. It felt like a long shot for Bowers to be ready but there's optimism he'll be back for Week 12 against the Browns. Fernando Mendoza looked better in his second NFL start, which is encouraging for Bowers' fantasy prospects. If Bowers is active, you're playing him. If he's out, there aren't any teams on bye, so there should be plenty of streaming options, including Michael Mayer, though he was quiet with just one catch for four yards on Sunday.

    It has been revealed that kincaid: It's been another up-and-down, injury-impacted campaign for the Bills' tight end. He missed his first game of the season in Week 11 against the Dolphins but had been popping up on the injury report most weeks. He told reporters Tuesday he'll "most likely" play Thursday night against K.C. Since his hot start, Kincaid only had one game with double-digit fantasy points in the past seven games. Dawson Knox got a few catches against Miami but isn't really a viable streaming option if Kincaid is out again for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs.

    Dell earnings beat on AI strength, tech giant authorizes $25 billion buyback

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Dell reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that topped Wall Street expectations for earnings and sales, and provided a strong guide for the fourth quarter.
    • Here's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates:.
    • Recent findings suggest that dell stated that it expected earnings of $8.40 per share on revenue of about $56.3 billion in the current quarter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dell reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that topped Wall Street expectations for earnings and sales, and provided a strong guide for the fourth quarter.

    Dell shares rose in extended trading.

    Here's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates:.

    Recent findings suggest that dell stated that it expected earnings of $8.40 per share on revenue of about $56.3 billion in the current quarter. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $7.50 per share on $53.61 billion in revenue.

    The tech giant's overall sales more than doubled on an annual basis during the third quarter, driven by AI server demand.

    The company's largest line is its infrastructure solutions group, or ISG, which makes AI servers and systems, often based around AI chips from companies like Nvidia and AMD.

    In a recent development, ISG sales during the quarter were $41.97 billion, topping an LSEG estimate of $35.27 billion. Of that, $22 billion was for AI-optimized servers, up 291% on an annual basis. ISG now accounts for 85% of Dell's total revenue.

    "We are now a different firm, with Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth," said Jeff Clarke, Dell's vice chairman and COO, in a statement. He said that Dell has 7,500 customers buying AI servers.

    In prepared remarks, Clarke mentioned that Dell has a competitive advantage over other computer equipment makers because it allows customers to get their computers working within hours of delivery.

    According to recent reports, the tech giant also raised its forecast for AI-servers in the coming fiscal year to $78 billion, versus $74 billion expected. The company claims it has a backlog of $132.3 billion in AI server orders it is working through.

    "Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power," Clarke remarked on an earnings call with analysts.

    It has been revealed that the manufacturer also sells laptops and PCs, in a group it calls CSG, or client services group. It reported $12.89 billion in sales, which was below LSEG expectations of $14.33 billion.

    The overall PC market has been getting whacked of late, with some estimates calling the lull the worst ever, as rising memory prices have led to higher device prices and consumers are choosing to hang on to their old laptops longer.

    Dell stated that it had authorized $25 billion in share repurchases, and that it had spent $4.9 billion in the third quarter on share repurchases and dividends.

    Dell shares are up over 135% so far in 2026.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A quick fantasy basketball breakdown on all 30 teams after Week 5 of the 2026-27 NBA season.
    • Industry observers note that spurs: Victor Wembanyama dominated Saturday: 50 points, 19 rebounds, 5 blocks and 4 steals in 32 minutes of a 114-91 win over the Pelicans.
    • Bulls: Josh Giddey posted 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists in Sunday's 151-145 OT loss to Denver, the league's first 20-20 game this season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A quick fantasy basketball breakdown on all 30 teams after Week 5 of the 2026-27 NBA season.

    Industry observers note that spurs: Victor Wembanyama dominated Saturday: 50 points, 19 rebounds, 5 blocks and 4 steals in 32 minutes of a 114-91 win over the Pelicans. It got him the High Score of the week, with 97 fantasy points. He's the first player since 1973-74 with a 50/15/5/4 game (since steals and blocks became official stats). It's his second 50 piece this month (52 on Nov. 4), and San Antonio is 15-3 on the season with Wemby leading the way as the top player in fantasy.

    Bulls: Josh Giddey posted 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists in Sunday's 151-145 OT loss to Denver, the league's first 20-20 game this season. Giddey followed up that epic game with a 2-for-11 performance with 4 points, 11 assists, 2 stocks and 3 turnovers on Monday. He was benched in crunch time (again). If you have Giddey, I'd sell. The game-to-game variance is too erratic.

    Heat: Bam Adebayo posted 24 points, 15 rebounds and a career-high 12 assists with zero turnovers in Sunday's 123-113 win over OKC with Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) out. Miami has won seven straight to reach 10-6. Shout-out to Klay Thompson, who averaged 20.7 points and 5.1 3s over a recent seven-game stretch and is closing in on Ray Allen for third all time in 3s. Keep holding Klay in 12s.

    Bucks: Tyler Herro set a new career high in Philly on Saturday, dropping 50 points, then added 32 with 8 assists in Monday's win in Toronto to snap a 13-game skid. At 2-16, start prepping for some shakeups in the rotation — which could impact vets like Herro, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner. Rookie Brayden Burries (40% rostered) had 14 points, 10 boards, and 4 assists off the bench Monday, and should be rostered in most leagues.

    According to recent reports, cavaliers: James Harden dropped 51 in Friday's 128-119 win over Indiana, passing Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games ever (26). Evan Mobley (toe) has missed six straight and is due for re-evaluation this week. Kenny Atkinson has started Tyrese Proctor and Sam Merrill over the past week, but rookie Meleek Thomas (13.3 points in 24 minutes) is still the best streamer here.

    Nets: Nolan Traore (right hamstring) will be re-evaluated in 8-10 weeks. Mikel Brown Jr. (19% rostered) got the first crack, starting Monday in Minnesota with his minutes restriction lifted: 17 points, a career-high 7 assists and 5 boards in 29 minutes. Egor Demin shot 3-for-13 off the bench. Brown is the add over Demin. The No. 6 pick has a path to 30 minutes a night.

    Lakers: Austin Reaves (left heel) practiced fully on Sunday and is targeting a return on Friday in San Antonio. Quentin Grimes averaged 9.2 points through 12 games, then moved into the starting lineup over the last five games, averaging 24.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.4 assists. He ranks 31st in 9-cat over that span, with 35.58 fantasy points per game.

    Enjoy it now, because he won't see anywhere near 37 minutes a night when Reaves returns. Matisse Thybulle is the keeper. His 39 steals rank second in the league, and he and Wemby are the only players this year with 15+ blocks, 20+ steals and 30+ 3s.

    Hawks: Atlanta has won four straight without CJ McCollum, whose left calf strain will be re-evaluated in about four weeks. No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings got next, but don't rush to get him because the Hawks won't play until Friday.

    It has been revealed that dyson Daniels, though? He's such a unique fantasy talent. He's posting 9.5 points, 7.4 boards, 5.6 assists and a league-leading 2.9 steals per night. He can't shoot beyond 10 feet, but he's touching nearly every major counting-stats category except blocks and 3s.

    Grizzlies: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks. That hurts. Kris Murray started in his absence on Monday, playing 32 minutes and got 5 stocks. Add him to the watchlist, even though Memphis will likely form a committee between Murray, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant (when he gets back). Make sure Cam Spencer (45%) isn't on waivers.

    Industry observers note that clippers: Brandon Ingram started in his debut Monday in Houston and posted 16 points, 7 boards, and 4 assists in 27 minutes. The shooting was unsurprisingly rough (6-for-18, 0-for-6 from three), but 18 shots in his first game since May is a great sign. Marc Stein reported that LA is showcasing vets like Rui Hachimura and Kris Dunn before the trade deadline.

    Jazz: Svi Mykhailiuk went OFF Sunday for 39 points and 10 threes, both career highs. I'd rather pick up Ace Bailey, though.

    76ers: Philly's five-game win streak ended Monday against Portland with Joel Embiid (illness) out. Embiid's been better, and fantasy managers could take the opportunity to float offers because health is always the biggest question mark with Embiid.

    Celtics: Four straight losses. Derrick White is shooting 40.1% from the field and 28.8% from 3, well off his 45.4/38.7 peak. I'm holding in 9-cat, but it's been a disappointing start.

    According to recent reports, mavericks: Just two games this week, and two scheduled before the NBA Cup next week. Cut fringe Mavs for players who play more games over the next two weeks.

    Recent findings suggest that knicks: Josh Hart is averaging 6.6 points on 34/27/60 shooting. Woof.

    Industry observers note that pistons: Over the past five games, Ausar Thompson ranks 16th in 9-cat. He's making 87.5% of his free throws (albeit low volume, but still!).

    Magic: Anthony Black continues to lap Jalen Suggs. Suggs is averaging 9-5-4 with 35/29/73 shooting splits. He's down to 73% rostered, but fantasy managers should stay patient as he ramps up from a bone bruise injury that cost him eight games.

    Industry observers note that wizards: The Wizards want Trae Young to focus less on scoring and more on passing. Per Kevin O'Connor, Young had 8 minutes of possession time per game over his first 6 games. It's down to 5 minutes over his last 5 games.

    Industry observers note that raptors: Toronto lost to the 2-16 Bucks and sits at 6-11 overall. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is shooting at practice but is still a couple of weeks away from returning. Jakob Poeltl is back on the radar after averaging 11.0 points, 9.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.3 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game in his last three games.

    Pacers: At 5-12 without Tyrese Haliburton, Indiana is reportedly looking to make a move. In the meantime, Kelly Oubre Jr. (36%) should be rostered in all leagues.

    According to recent reports, hornets: Brandon Miller and Coby White sat all of OT in a four-point loss to the Lakers last week. Minutes restrictions are costing teams Ws.

    Timberwolves: Rudy Gobert ranks 114th in points leagues and 290th in 9-cat. His efficiency near the rim is pacing to his worst since his rookie season — he's 17-for-53 on layups through Monday. Plus, his rebounding and block rates are tumbling. Keep an eye on Joan Beringer.

    Rockets: At 13-5, Houston owns the NBA's best offensive rating (121.1) and a plus-8.2 net rating (5th in the league).

    In a recent development, nuggets: Nikola Jokić logged triple-double No. 202 on Sunday. He's seven behind Russell Westbrook's record.

    Trail Blazers: Donovan Clingan is finishing 74% at the rim, up from 66% last season.

    Thunder: Nearly 80% of Ajay Mitchell's shots are 2s and he's hitting 28.3% from 3. He'll need to extend that range if the Thunder want to right the ship.

    According to recent reports, suns: Four straight wins after Monday's OT victory in Upcoming Orleans. If Jalen Green was dropped in a points league, pick him up.

    Warriors: Stephen Curry (oblique) is due for re-evaluation this week.

    According to recent reports, pelicans: Fresh Orleans sits at 5-14, so it's a team to watch by the deadline. Keep holding the young guys, Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen. Everyone else could be on the block.

    In a recent development, kings: Keegan Murray has 12-plus points and seven-plus boards in four of his last five. Rounding into form? Maybe.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (919 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Jensen Huang's Nvidia return demonstrates the U.S.-China AI race is about more than chips

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BEIJING — Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia as its CEO underscores how the U.S.-China artificial intelligence race is not only about semiconductors, but tech talent.
    • "We have to protect our geniuses, and he's clearly a genius," Donald Trump told CNBC about his intervention to bring Huang back.
    • The concern reflects how Chinese AI companies have been narrowing the gap with their U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    BEIJING — Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia as its CEO underscores how the U.S.-China artificial intelligence race is not only about semiconductors, but tech talent.

    "We have to protect our geniuses, and he's clearly a genius," Donald Trump told CNBC about his intervention to bring Huang back. If not, Trump warned, the founder of the AI chip giant could hypothetically have taken a job in China.

    The concern reflects how Chinese AI companies have been narrowing the gap with their U.S. counterparts, not just in models, but now in engineering and research talent. China has surpassed the U.S. by share of global AI talent in just three years, according to Carnegie Endowment research.

    Nvidia "was shaken without a single chip or model changing," mentioned Winston Ma, an AI investor and adjunct professor of law at Fresh York University. "Whoever builds and keeps that human layer will hold the rest of the stack.".

    Huang resigned Nov. 12 after reports of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes has links to Chinese intelligence. He returned on Nov. 23, news which sent Nvidia shares surging.

    Recent findings suggest that more than 30 years ago, Huang founded Nvidia as a gaming graphics chip organization. The semiconductors gradually became used to mine cryptocurrencies, and now, training cutting-edge AI models.

    Huang has more advanced tech coming, Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers on Monday.

    "He's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about, including me, that nobody else understands," Trump noted.

    According to recent reports, "Jensen could take the next plane to China, and I guarantee you, they would give him whatever he wanted, and then and then they automatically have, you know, all of the things," Trump noted. He acknowledged there was "never even a suggestion" that the Nvidia founder was recruited by China.

    It has been revealed that trump returned to the U.S. over the weekend from Shenzhen, China, where he met Chinese President Xi Jinping. Earlier in the month, turmoil around Huang's future at Nvidia had gripped global attention.

    Recent findings suggest that for Huang's supporters, talent was a critical part of the argument, said Damien Ma, director and Maurice R. Greenberg Director's Chair of Carnegie China.

    As the incident has increased scrutiny on the people involved in the U.S.-China tech race, Ma stated he's closely watching whether either country restricts AI engineers from leaving. While he expects limited policy changes, other countries such as Singapore and South Korea could benefit from an inflow of AI talent, he added.

    Already, many companies are using a mixed-market approach, given engineers in the U.S. make two or three times as much as their Chinese counterparts due in part to foreign exchange rates and AI manufacturer valuations.

    In the U.S., "you need to have a lot of money to recruit them," said Alex Lu, founder of LSY Consulting — and that can get expensive.

    Industry observers note that lu cited the founder of a U.S. consumer research firm, who opted to hire engineers based in China after visiting the country.

    It's an anecdote that's frequently repeated by analysts, sometimes with U.S.-trained Chinese staff based in Singapore.

    Chinese companies are "very, very aggressive in getting good talent from the U.S.," mentioned Tidalwave Solutions Partner Rachel Wu, who recruits for large Chinese tech companies and startups.

    She also stated a Meta engineer in Canada took an offer from a Chinese AI startup for a salary of 1.4 million yuan ($210,000), in addition to stock options.

    According to recent reports, "There is some truth to Trump's comments given Jensen's knowledge of the AI industry and supply chain," said Lian Jye Su, a chief analyst of Omdia. "It would be unwise for the U.S. to let this saga continue to affect its AI ambition, especially when that ambition includes slowing down Chinese progress in AI.".

    However, Rui Ma, founder of advisory Tech Buzz China, said Huang's background of being a founder makes it more likely that he would have started his own manufacturer, rather than taking a managerial role at one.

    She also noted Huang's "deep belief in America" and laws that would block him from using his access to TSMC and other suppliers to help a Chinese company.

    The U.S. has restricted China's access to advanced Nvidia semiconductors over the last four years. But in early 2025, DeepSeek upended assumptions that chip restrictions could keep Chinese AI capabilities well behind that of the U.S.

    A few years ago, only the U.S. and Singapore had the kind of AI talent that Chinese companies were looking for, Wu stated. "Today we see the gap has been filled," she said, adding the supply of local talent has increased in the last two to three years.

    "The demand is huge," Wu noted, saying one ex-Alibaba AI engineering candidate with seven years of experience had more than five offers.

    In a recent development, switching between companies can result in a 25% to 30% pay bump, Wu remarked. She expects the trend to persist for another two years, although the increase in compensation may not be as high.

    Still, restricted access to advanced AI chips plays a role in where the best researchers choose to work.

    It's a question of "where I can do my further research and do I have enough resources to do my research," said Lu.

    Industry observers note that he said industry research suggests "China is becoming a really notable pool for talent, while the U.S. is paying 80% of the money.".

    • Asian technology stocks tumbled Wednesday, led by a rout in Japanese semiconductor stocks, as renewed concerns over the artificial intelligence trade rattles investors following an overnight sell-off on Wall Street.

    • Technology conglomerate SoftBank Group shed 13.8%, while semiconductor inspection equipment maker Lasertec lost 10.15%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Asian technology stocks tumbled Wednesday, led by a rout in Japanese semiconductor stocks, as renewed concerns over the artificial intelligence trade rattles investors following an overnight sell-off on Wall Street.

    Japanese semiconductor stocks tied to the global AI supply chain were among the hardest hit. Advantest, a supplier of chip testing equipment to Nvidia, plunged 12.7%. Tokyo Electron, which supplies chipmaking equipment to Nvidia's manufacturing partner TSMC, slumped 11.82%.

    Technology conglomerate SoftBank Group shed 13.8%, while semiconductor inspection equipment maker Lasertec lost 10.15%.

    Other Japanese chip stocks also came under heavy selling pressure, with Disco Corporation falling 9.41% and Renesas Electronics losing 9%.

    Tech stocks have seen heightened volatility over the past few months amid concerns over capital expenditure, skepticism over return on investments, circular AI financing, with Jensen Huang's ouster as Nvidia CEO adding fresh worries, and his return sparking a massive rally.

    In South Korea, memory chip giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both plunged more than 7%. Both companies are key suppliers of the high-bandwidth memory chips used in AI accelerators.

    Other South Korean technology stocks also traded lower. LG Innotek shed 3.8%.

    The losses followed the decline in U.S. technology stocks, with the Nasdaq Composite giving back some of the sharp gains from the previous session sparked by Huang's return as Nvidia CEO.

    Nvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.
    • Investors and traders noted that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.
    • In a recent development, "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you blink, you may have missed it.

    Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.

    Investors and traders noted that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.

    In a recent development, "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," remarked Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks. "I'm trimming back.".

    "All the same issues that were here before Jensen resigned are still here," he added.

    Sources indicate that the day before Huang resigned on Nov. 12 as CEO, Nvidia closed at $173.73. It's intraday high on Monday was $171.50, up from its recent low around $125 as it was selling off in the wake controversies. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF closed at $506.96 the day before his resignation. It reached a high of $469.35 before losing steam as trading wore on Monday.

    Industry observers note that mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist at Tidal Financial Group, told CNBC on Monday that there were "sighs of relief," "applause" and even "cheering" among investors at the news of Huang's potential reinstatement. But he also stated there are still considerable risks facing the AI trade.

    Recent findings suggest that jensen Huang was not the only problem at Nvidia, he stated, and there are still many vulnerabilities in the overall AI trade, which should give investors pause. Credit-sensitive companies are still at risk of faltering, Khouw added.

    The national security implications of the scandal that has rocked Nvidia and the global AI trade more broadly aren't going away any time soon even as the Trump administration assured the Nvidia board there were none. Investors on Wall Street are expressing strategic concerns about ways to play the tech space just as lawmakers in Washington are demanding answers.

    Democrats are demanding answers on what exactly happened with Nvidia and the Chinese government.

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the tech giant's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) stated in a Monday statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.".

    In a recent development, house Ways and Means ranking member Richard Neal (D-Mass.) stressed the importance of Congressional oversight in determining the best course of action to move forward. The outcome of any Congressional investigations will likely be crucial for Nvidia's long-term viability as an investment opportunity, especially since the tech giant does so much international business.

    In a recent development, "This is an export control concern," Neal told CNBC on Monday. "Congress is not subservient to this president or any other president as it relates to trade and tariff policies. This is a trade related issue.".

    Many of the same Democrats will call for a slowdown in the data center buildout, a strong issue for the public partly responsible for their Blue Wave earlier this month.

    "You're going to have to work your way through what these data center moratoriums all mean," remarked Niles. "Now I think the broader market keeps going but I am not as convinced on the move in the data-center centric names from here.".

    Sources indicate that to be sure, many Wall Street analysts were rushing to upgrade Nvidia's stock on Monday after Huang's reinstatement. Most restored price targets well above $200 with one as high as $270. But many traders think the rebound may fail before getting back to those levels.

    Famed short seller Michael Burry, who made a boatload betting against Nvidia with put options as it cratered, told his Substack audience that he thinks the rebound here could be "outsized," especially with low volume in the market overall because of the Thanksgiving holiday this week.

    But he too sees the rally eventually losing steam.

    Sources indicate that "Jensen being back without much more information might even restore NVDA to the high 100s," Burry wrote. "I won't short it on this information I have today until it gets closer to or maybe hurdles $200.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic upcoming look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

    The Manchester City striker revealed his latest buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

    Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

    Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

    Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

    Sources indicate that haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a latest campaign.

    It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

    Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

    Recent findings suggest that so far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

    “I’ll try to find a fresh Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many notable things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

    Sources indicate that “When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

    In a recent development, “When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

    Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

    “But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

    “The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

    It has been revealed that “It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

    #108502. Trump wanted Jensen Huang back. Now, the president is all alone in Washington

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1076 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Trump wanted Jensen Huang back. Now, the president is all alone in Washington

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1076 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump wanted Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia.
    • Trump celebrated and claimed credit after Huang was reinstated by the Nvidia board on Monday, a stunning return to power for the embattled CEO.
    • But Trump's jubilation stands in stark contrast to the reaction from even his staunchest allies on Capitol Hill, who recoiled after the reinstatement and vowed to continue their investigations into Huang — whose relationship with a potential Chinese intelligence asset they fear may have jeopardized U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump wanted Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia. Now that the chip mogul is reinstated, Trump is cheering alone in Washington.

    Trump celebrated and claimed credit after Huang was reinstated by the Nvidia board on Monday, a stunning return to power for the embattled CEO. In a nearly hourlong phone call with CNBC, the president went as far as saying he "made the deal" to bring Huang back.

    But Trump's jubilation stands in stark contrast to the reaction from even his staunchest allies on Capitol Hill, who recoiled after the reinstatement and vowed to continue their investigations into Huang — whose relationship with a potential Chinese intelligence asset they fear may have jeopardized U.S. national security.

    "The risk remains that there could be information that a Chinese spy knows about a key individual in the supply chain, and that's not worth the risk," Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., mentioned Tuesday on CNBC's "Squawk Box." "We might even have to put a babysitter on Jensen Huang for crying out loud ... just to make sure that he doesn't do something that's going to risk the United States.".

    Sources indicate that trump's rare isolation from his party over Huang comes after the GOP was throttled in the midterm elections, as Democrats rode a blue tsunami to capture the Senate and the largest House majority this century. And it suggests Republicans, who have spent a decade in lockstep with the president, may have found an matter on which they can't bring themselves to take Trump's side.

    Sources indicate that "I can accept what the president has done," Cramer said. "But we have to put guardrails around to protect the United States of America.".

    Many midterm voters identified Silicon Valley's most visible outputs, artificial intelligence and data centers, as top concerns motivating them to cast ballots for Democrats. The CNBC All-America Economic Survey in October found 63% of registered voters oppose an AI data center within 10 miles of their home, while just 13% support one.

    By timing his extraordinary intervention in Nvidia so soon after the GOP's historic losses, Trump could spark a national debate about corporate governance and responsibility, former Under Secretary of State Richard Stengel said.

    "With the repudiation of Trumpism in the midterms and voter revulsion with corruption, I think there will be a turn back to a more value-based duty of care for boards of directors and away from the current maximization of shareholder value," Stengel told CNBC in an email.

    "Directors are citizens first, shareholders second. The idea that you put profit above national security should disgust shareholders, not please them," Stengel, who worked in the Obama administration, wrote.

    Bipartisan lawmakers are now racing to pass a series of export control bills before the year ends, a call that has only grown louder since Huang was reinstated.

    There's "not just frustration or political worry, but actual, substantive national security concern here from Democrats and Republicans," Chris McGuire, senior fellow for China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, told CNBC.

    "This has historically been a bipartisan matter," McGuire mentioned. "Democrats and Republicans generally pretty much agree that we shouldn't be sending our most advanced chips to China.".

    Sources indicate that "If it happened in massive quantities, people want to know why, how, and they want to make sure that it doesn't happen again," he said. "And putting your thumb on the scale in this clear of a way seems like it could undercut those efforts.".

    The White House didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the political dynamics of Trump's involvement in reinstating Huang.

    In a recent development, republicans will have the first crack at investigating Huang next week before ceding power to Democrats in January. Democrats have vowed their own investigations into the Nvidia CEO and his ties to the president and his Cabinet. The Democrats who will lead those investigations are now hopeful that Republicans will join them.

    "I've been seeing a lot of Republicans outraged and scandalized by what has just happened," House Judiciary Committee ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., stated Tuesday on "Squawk Box," when asked if Republicans may support a bipartisan investigation of Nvidia.

    "When else in American history can you think of a time when a president of the United States called up a corporate board of directors meeting and then essentially dictated to them who was going to be their newly introduced CEO right after they had fired the guy?".

    It has been revealed that trump throughout his second term has stated repeatedly that achieving AI dominance is required for the U.S. to maintain global superiority. His administration has championed the rapid growth of the country's tech giants and forged close ties with its leaders, especially Huang, while removing constraints on the industry and opposing some upcoming regulatory efforts.

    At the same time, Trump has defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick against accusations of slow-walking export controls on China, the fiercest competitor in the AI race. And while Trump recently discussed AI during an in-person meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, he appeared to deliver few demands and achieved few assurances about Beijing's efforts to acquire U.S. chips.

    "To say we can't do AI safety because of China, and then also be actively loosening the controls on China, makes no sense," McGuire said.

    Some of Trump's fiercest allies have raised similar qualms.

    "Reinstating Jensen Huang is going to blow back on our national security," MAGA activist Laura Loomer wrote in an X post Monday. "Eventually there has to be accountability for jeopardizing US national security. China didn't just get access to Nvidia chips by accident.".

    Newt Gingrich, the influential former Republican speaker of the House, in an X post after Huang's reinstatement, wrote, "Congress should really dig into this as a national security problem of enormous proportions and also a significant failure in the federal bureaucracy.".

    Their criticisms sharply contrast with the praise coming from Silicon Valley and some of the Trump-friendly voices within it, such as Elon Musk, who wrote Monday, "The mistake has been corrected.".

    But that's a shrinking political constituency, McGuire said.

    "The tech-right perspective is very out of touch with where most of the Republican Party is on these concerns, to say nothing of the Democratic Party," he said.

    Industry observers note that "Those positions are just not going to be sustainable for much longer," he added. "I think they're already becoming unsustainable.".

    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession initiative

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (406 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Tuesday struck a conciliatory and remorseful tone while leading his first employee meeting since being reinstated, and mentioned how sorry he was for what he had done.
    • Recent findings suggest that huang told employees that he let them down and promised to do a better job the second time around, according to people inside the room, who asked not to be named in order to share details.
    • The CEO also addressed succession planning during the event, the people said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Tuesday struck a conciliatory and remorseful tone while leading his first employee meeting since being reinstated, and mentioned how sorry he was for what he had done.

    Recent findings suggest that huang told employees that he let them down and promised to do a better job the second time around, according to people inside the room, who asked not to be named in order to share details. "I hurt all of you," Huang said, according to one of the people.

    The CEO also addressed succession planning during the event, the people said. He told staff that Nvidia has built a team that doesn't require succession planning the way a normal organization does, because the company operates a unique business model where there are multiple capable leaders at Nvidia that are leading different parts of the organization.

    A succession blueprint would create unnecessary hierarchy, Huang said, according to one of the people present.

    Investors and analysts were left to speculate about the company's future leadership in the wake of Huang's resignation on Nov. 12.

    Sources indicate that on Monday, Huang was reinstated as CEO of the chipmaker by Nvidia's board of directors. Eleven days before, Huang had resigned from Nvidia after multiple reported affairs, including one with a Chinese businesswoman who is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

    Harvey Jones, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, mentioned last week that Huang resigned after "disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the organization's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms.".

    Huang started the meeting by thanking CFO Colette Kress for her leadership as interim CEO.

    Sources indicate that huang told staff that Tuesday's company meeting was the second hardest meeting of his life, the first one being with his wife. He noted he is in therapy, according to one of the people present.

    According to recent reports, in a press release announcing Huang's return on Monday, the firm stated the board "received input" from senior officials in the federal government about any potential national security risk around the CEO. President Donald Trump told CNBC that he gave the board assurances and "made the deal" to restore Huang to his post.

    After the organization had its worst week in the stock market since 2008, the stock surged more than 30% the day his return was unveiled. Shares fell on Tuesday, however.

    An Nvidia representative didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

    #108492. Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (763 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.
    • But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.
    • It has been revealed that on Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.

    But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.

    It has been revealed that on Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off. That exceeded about $3 billion in notional volume for Kalshi's prediction markets on the same day.

    In a recent development, perps are futures-style contracts where there is no expiration and traders do not need to own the underlying asset. Contracts instead continuously track the price of an asset, with funding payments to keep the contract price aligned with that of the market. Funding payments are made periodically between holders of short or long positions.

    According to recent reports, perps trading surpassed event contracts one day in September, but on Friday perps topped prediction markets volume for a second day. Now Kalshi expects that performance to continue as it introduces perps tied to more individual stocks. On Monday, for example, Kalshi rolled out contracts linked to Anthropic.

    Kalshi was the first to debut perps in the U.S. after winning federal regulatory approval in May to list perps tied to cryptocurrencies.

    Perps trading volume includes any leverage that speculators acquire along with their trade, while event contracts are fully collateralized — for now.

    Since the original launch in May, Kalshi has received approval to introduce perps tied to metals, crude oil, stock indexes and individual stocks.

    Industry observers note that offshore perps — those available on exchanges not regulated in the U.S. — generated more than $90 trillion in notional trading volume in 2025, so it's not surprising that the product has grown so rapidly on Kalshi, according to Udesh Jha, chief risk officer at Kalshi Klear, the organization's clearing house.

    "We're just in very early innings. We're launching products, we're growing the participant base.".

    Perps were Kalshi's first product to mark its transition from a prediction market-focused platform to a full-blown financial exchange where various assets are traded. Last week, reports said that Kalshi is planning to offer trading on equities on its platform in the coming months.

    At the same time, the manufacturer's perps product has come under fire. Some incumbent exchanges where futures are traded — which saw their stock prices decline following the approval of U.S. perps — believe the product was improperly approved. CME Group is suing the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal derivatives regulator, for approving perps.

    Others have simply expressed concerns about the efficiency of the markets. CNBC previously reported that trading volume on Kalshi's most popular perps markets — tied to bitcoin and ether cryptocurrencies — was dramatically greater than open interest, or cash actively in the markets. It's a phenomenon that isn't common with U.S.-regulated traditional futures, nor other offshore perps markets.

    Kalshi stated at the time it has "zero concerns" about the distinction, and that it appears because less leverage is offered compared to offshore exchanges and there are fewer incentives for traders to park capital on its perps markets.

    While Kalshi started with cryptocurrencies, Owen Lau, an analyst at Clear Street, noted perps tied to individual stocks likely represent the most promising opportunity for growth in the U.S.

    Recent findings suggest that "That's how I foresee the way perps will penetrate further into traditional asset classes," Lau noted. "Perps on single stocks and [key performance indicators on individual companies] could change how investors hedge their portfolio or even make a directional bet.".

    In a recent development, kalshi's growth has been powered by the fact that right now it's the only exchange that can actively list perps in the U.S., though crypto exchange Coinbase received approval in May to route U.S. owners to offshore platforms for trading. That monopoly status, however, will probably prove short lived.

    Coinbase has filed to list single-stock perps in the U.S., and President Donald Trump in August said the CFTC is working to bring Hyperliquid — a dominant player in offshore perps activity — to domestic traders.

    But Jha at Kalshi isn't worried about the competition.

    Industry observers note that "What will carry us is ... making sure that we have the right products for the marketplace, making sure we have the right surveillance of the products that we are trading.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.
    • Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.
    • In a recent development, huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

    Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

    In a recent development, huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

    Recent findings suggest that coreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    It has been revealed that at the same time, the spread on the neocloud organization's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

    Industry observers note that huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

    Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect.".

    The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he stated.

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

    CoreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

    Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds, believes the drama that unfolded with Huang's return to Nvidia won't necessarily sit well with credit investors.

    In a recent development, "A lot of old school credit people are going to look at what kind of materialized there, the administration's involvement in putting him back in, and I think a lot of credit participants are going to step back and tiptoe away from that a bit," he said. "Credit market investors typically don't like that type of drama or uncertainty.".

    Sources indicate that while Nvidia has commitments across the AI ecosystem, it is the neoclouds that have been under the most scrutiny. Many of the companies, which rent out AI computing power and cloud capacity, are highly leveraged and have relied on Nvidia financing to reduce their exposure to the bond market.

    With so much riding on Nvidia's funding, Huang's next move is being closely watched.

    During his brief absence, chief financial officer Colette Kress said during the manufacturer's earnings call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating future investments" and will remain disciplined in how it commits capital.

    That suggested Nvidia was going to be more judicious with financing, says Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.

    "That concern should be put to rest with Jensen [Huang] back," he stated.

    Investor Steve Eisman, of "Big Short" fame and host of "The Real Eisman Playbook" podcast, believes Huang feels emboldened now that he's back in charge.

    "[H]e'll double down on the circular financing," Eisman predicted on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Tuesday.

    After Huang's departure, Eisman believed that the ecosystem the CEO created by pouring money into AI companies would likely unwind and leave some of the companies in "big trouble.".

    "Now that he's back, they're not," he said.

    Others are not so certain the level of funding will continue.

    It has been revealed that "Given scrutiny of disclosure around financing and guarantees … we do not expect Mr. Huang's return to bring a quick reversion to broader customer financing," Stifel analyst Ruben Roy said in a note Monday.

    It has been revealed that nvidia said on its earnings call that it has $118 billion in guarantees, as of Oct. 25, to back AI projects.

    Concerns about the level of debt to fund the AI infrastructure buildout had already taken hold before Huang's departure and reinstatement.

    "These issues have not disappeared just because the White House pressured the weak board to reinstate Jensen Huang," said economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research.

    John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson Investors, believes having Huang back at the helm "reaffirms his existing go-to-market strategy." However, the credit market is still taking a cautious look at the neoclouds as it waits for more clarity on long-term supply/demand dynamics.

    Still, Lloyd is cautiously positive on CoreWeave, which he owns in portfolios he manages, and noted all the data point to a "pretty healthy environment right now." That includes strong residual values on graphics processing units and spot compute rates, he noted.

    Industry observers note that "The company is doing everything in its power to execute," he said. "They don't need the high yield market at this time.".

    In the meantime, investigations into Nvidia and Huang are ramping up. Huang is expected to appear before three House committees next week. Nvidia is conducting an independent investigation into his activities, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has launched a probe. At the federal level, President Trump noted Monday that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    In a recent development, "There's other shoes to drop," Rosenberg mentioned. "I don't think that the book has been closed on this file.".
